gloss_en: how German builds the numbers above twelve
source_note: Forms from the Wortgruppenliste, Zahlen. The explanation is written for this app and needs review.

payload.explanation_en: Learn one to twelve as single words. From 13 to 19 say the unit and then zehn: dreizehn. The tens end in zig: zwanzig, vierzig, but dreißig has ß. From 21 to 99 the unit comes first, joined with und: einundzwanzig, fünfunddreißig. Hundreds and thousands come before that: hunderteins, zweihundert, dreihundertfünfzig, zweitausendvierzehn. A number below a million is written as one word.

payload.explanation_en: From 1 to 19 add te to the number: vierte, zehnte, neunzehnte. From 20 on add ste: zwanzigste, einunddreißigste. Four forms are irregular: erste, dritte, siebte and achte, which has only one t. An ordinal takes an adjective ending. In a date it is der erste März after ist, and am ersten März when you say when something happens. In figures an ordinal is the number with a full stop: der 1. März, am 12. April.

payload.note: um is only for clock times. Without Uhr after halb and Viertel: um halb acht, um Viertel nach neun.

source_note: Alphabetische Wortliste, example sentence under müssen. The list has Ich muss jeden Tag von 8 Uhr bis 18 Uhr arbeiten.

payload.slot: a start and an end: two days or two clock times

examples.text: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag.
examples.gloss_en: I work from Monday to Friday.

examples.text: Der Kurs ist von neun bis zwölf Uhr.
examples.gloss_en: The course is from nine to twelve o'clock.

payload.note: This frame has two slots, the start after von and the end after bis.

source_note: Alphabetische Wortliste, example sentence under Uhr. The list has Es ist vier Uhr.

payload.slot: the hour, and the minutes after Uhr if there are any
payload.note: Official times use the 24 hour clock: dreizehn Uhr. One o'clock is ein Uhr, not eins Uhr.

gloss_en: It is half past ... (the hour before the one named)
source_note: Wortgruppenliste, Uhrzeit. The list prints halb drei.

payload.note: Name the hour that is coming, not the hour that has passed.

source_note: Wortgruppenliste, Uhrzeit. The list prints Viertel vor/nach zwei.

payload.slot: the hour that has just passed

examples.gloss_en: It is a quarter past two.
It is a quarter past ten.

payload.note: Minutes work the same way: fünf Minuten nach eins, zehn nach acht.

source_note: Wortgruppenliste, Uhrzeit. The list prints Viertel vor/nach zwei.

examples.gloss_en: It is a quarter to two.
It is a quarter to nine.

payload.note: Minutes work the same way: fünf Minuten vor eins, zehn vor acht.

source_note: Wortgruppenliste, Datum. The list prints heute ist der 1. März = heute ist der erste März.

payload.slot: the date: an ordinal ending in e, then the month

examples.gloss_en: Today is the first of March.
Today is the twelfth of April.

payload.note: In figures: Heute ist der 1. März. The full stop makes the number an ordinal.

source_note: The sentence itself is not printed in the Goethe A1 Wortliste. It is built from the A1 headwords wie, spät and sein. Needs a source on review.

examples.text: Entschuldigung, wie spät ist es? Es ist halb drei.
examples.gloss_en: Excuse me, what time is it? It is half past two.

source_note: The sentence itself is not printed in the Goethe A1 Wortliste. It is built from the A1 headwords wie viel, Uhr and sein. Needs a source on review.

examples.text: Wie viel Uhr ist es? Es ist zehn Uhr.
examples.gloss_en: What time is it? It is ten o'clock.

payload.note: Means the same as Wie spät ist es?
The verb after wer is singular: Wer kommt?
The list gives it as welch-. The ending follows the noun like der, die, das: welcher Tag, welche Sprache, welches Buch.

examples.gloss_en: How many children do you have?

payload.note: Written as two words. Before a plural noun it is wie viele: wie viele Kinder.

examples.text: Das ist mein Bruder. Er wohnt in Köln.
examples.gloss_en: That is my brother. He lives in Cologne.

payload.note: Also stands for a thing that is der: Der Kurs ist gut. Er beginnt um neun Uhr.

examples.text: Das ist Anna. Sie kommt aus Polen.
examples.gloss_en: That is Anna. She comes from Poland.

payload.note: With a verb ending in t it means she. Also stands for a thing that is die: Die Stadt ist schön. Sie heißt Hamburg.

examples.text: Das Kind ist klein. Es ist drei Jahre alt.
examples.gloss_en: The child is small. It is three years old.

payload.note: Stands for a das noun, and is the empty subject in sentences about weather and time: Es ist spät.

source_note: Not a headword of its own in the Goethe A1 Wortliste. The headword ihr/ihm/ihn there is the dative of sie. The pronoun for a group appears only in the example sentence under mitmachen: Warum macht ihr nicht mit? Needs a source on review.

payload.note: For two or more people you say du to. The verb ends in t: ihr kommt, ihr habt, ihr seid.

source_note: Alphabetische Wortliste, headword sie. The example printed there shows the singular. The plural sense is the same headword.

examples.text: Das sind meine Eltern. Sie leben in Indien.
examples.gloss_en: These are my parents. They live in India.

payload.note: With a verb ending in en and a small s it means they. With a capital S it is the formal you: Sie.

examples.text: Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?
examples.gloss_en: How do you say that in German?

payload.note: The verb has the er form. Do not mix it up with the noun der Mann.
mein before der and das nouns, meine before die nouns and plurals. In the accusative only the masculine changes: meinen Bruder.
Goes with du. Endings as for mein: dein Bruder, deine Schwester, deinen Bruder.

examples.text: Das ist Peter und das ist seine Frau.
examples.gloss_en: This is Peter and this is his wife.

payload.note: Goes with er and es. Looks like the verb sein but always stands before a noun. Endings as for mein.

source_note: Not a headword of its own in the Goethe A1 Wortliste. The possessive appears only in example sentences, for example under leben: Sie lebt bei ihrer Schwester. Needs a source on review.

examples.text: Das ist Anna und das ist ihr Mann.
examples.gloss_en: This is Anna and this is her husband.

examples.text: Anna und ihre Schwester wohnen in Köln.
examples.gloss_en: Anna and her sister live in Cologne.

examples.text: Die Kinder und ihre Eltern kommen heute.
examples.gloss_en: The children and their parents are coming today.

payload.note: Goes with sie, both for she and for they. Endings as for mein: ihr Mann, ihre Schwester.

examples.text: Unser Sohn ist zehn Jahre alt.
examples.gloss_en: Our son is ten years old.

payload.note: Goes with wir. Endings as for mein: unser Sohn, unsere Tochter.
Goes with ihr. With an ending the middle e drops out: eure Eltern, not euere.

source_note: Not a headword of its own in the Goethe A1 Wortliste. The formal possessive appears only in example sentences, for example under Postleitzahl: Wie ist Ihre Postleitzahl? Needs a source on review.

payload.note: Goes with Sie and always has a capital I. Endings as for mein: Ihr Name, Ihre Adresse.

examples.gloss_en: Are you coming today or tomorrow?
Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.text: Ich komme aus Indien, aber ich wohne in Berlin.
examples.gloss_en: I come from India, but I live in Berlin.

examples.text: Ich spreche Englisch, aber nur ein bisschen Deutsch.
examples.gloss_en: I speak English, but only a little German.

payload.note: A comma comes before aber. The word order after it stays the same: aber ich wohne.

examples.gloss_en: He is coming at seven o'clock.

examples.text: Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr.
examples.gloss_en: The course starts at nine o'clock.

payload.note: Takes the accusative. For clock times only: um acht Uhr, but am Montag and im Mai.

examples.text: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag.
examples.gloss_en: I work from Monday to Friday.

examples.text: Das ist ein Freund von mir.
examples.gloss_en: This is a friend of mine.

examples.text: Das ist die Mutter von Anna.

payload.note: Takes the dative. von dem becomes vom.
Often paired with von: von neun bis zwölf Uhr.

gloss_en: before, to (clock time); in front of

examples.gloss_en: I am coming before twelve o'clock.

payload.note: In clock times it counts the minutes to the next hour: fünf Minuten vor eins. With the dative it also means ago: vor einer Stunde.

gloss_en: after, past (clock time); to (a city or country)

examples.text: Es ist schon fünf nach zwölf.
examples.gloss_en: It is already five past twelve.

examples.text: Nach dem Kurs gehe ich nach Hause.
examples.gloss_en: After the course I go home.

payload.note: Takes the dative. For places it is used with cities and countries that have no article: nach Berlin, nach Indien.

gloss_en: since, for (a time that goes on until now)

examples.text: Ich wohne seit drei Jahren in Köln.
examples.gloss_en: I have been living in Cologne for three years.

examples.text: Ich lerne seit einem Monat Deutsch.
examples.gloss_en: I have been learning German for a month.

payload.note: Takes the dative, and German uses the present tense with it: Ich wohne seit einem Jahr hier.

examples.gloss_en: I am coming with my wife.

payload.note: Takes the dative: mit dem Bus, mit der Bahn, mit meinen Kindern.
Takes the accusative: für meinen Bruder, für mich.

examples.gloss_en: I am coming without my children.

payload.note: Takes the accusative: ohne meinen Mann, ohne dich.

gloss_en: at (a person's home, a company); near

examples.text: Mein Mann arbeitet bei der Post.
examples.gloss_en: My husband works at the post office.

payload.note: Takes the dative. bei dem becomes beim: beim Arzt.

examples.gloss_en: I am going to the doctor.
The bus goes to the station.

examples.text: Am Abend bin ich zu Hause.
examples.gloss_en: In the evening I am at home.

payload.note: Takes the dative. zu dem becomes zum, zu der becomes zur. zu Hause is a fixed phrase and means at home.

examples.text: Mein Kind ist noch ein Baby.
examples.gloss_en: My child is still a baby.
Do you have any more questions?

examples.text: Ich lerne schon ein Jahr Deutsch.
examples.gloss_en: I have already been learning German for a year.
